questions.finding: Management demand forecasts and interest in 2029/2030 orders support scarcity visibility, but do not prove conversion into recognized revenue. Existing risk disclosures explicitly preserve cancellation, delay, export and customer-capex uncertainty.

Q3 IBM sales of EUR3.289bn are material and above guidance, while FY2025 IBM sales were EUR8.193bn. This supports economic relevance but one above-guidance quarter cannot establish a durable growth rate or margin contribution.

Q3 2026 gross margin of 57.5% and FY2026 guidance around 56% are materially above FY2025 gross margin of 52.8%. The frozen thesis already notes IBM upside in Q3; therefore 57.5% must not be treated as normalized sustainable margin without additional cost/mix evidence.

2025 disclosures show four customers represented 61.2% of sales and China/Taiwan/South Korea each represented large sales shares. Export controls can change shipment eligibility and geographic mix. Scarcity at aggregate level therefore does not imply all backlog/demand is equally convertible.

No market valuation or subsequent return is authorized or needed for business-mechanism validation. A correct business mechanism cannot support an undervaluation or alpha claim under current authority.
